  running after `waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds` (default 60; 0 = kill
  switch) is auto-backgrounded — CONVERTED, never restarted (it already
  runs as a registry job under the soft-yield path): the pending tool call
  resolves exactly once with the backgrounded result (`bash_auto_background
  .dart` text, anchored on the hand-back sentence so the loop's stuck
  supervisor and budget ladder classify it as a real conversion), the
  settle notification stays armed, an explicit `timeout` at/below the
  threshold keeps the classic path while one above carries over as the
  job's cap, and hosts without `BackgroundShell` keep legacy behavior.
  Headless `fa -p` DRAINS live shell
  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared
  wall-clock ceiling `headless.shellJobDrainMs` (default 30 min; 0 =
  shell-job-scoped kill switch: live shell jobs detach at once while the
  pre-existing subagent drain stays unconditional), then the detach
  summary applies (gh-1459). The drain wrap-up also raises the
  settle→reaction fence: from `_finishHeadlessDrain` on, a job settle (or
  task completion) does bookkeeping only — no reaction run (gh-1589 I2).
  While the drain waits, every `headless.shellJobQuietMs`
  (default 5 min; 0 = off) of a still-running awaited job steers ONE
  interim liveness notice (`job <id> running · <elapsed> · tail: …` +
  the bash_job escape hatch), skipped for a crossing the model probed
  itself (`bash_job status/output` bumps the entry's probe generation)
  (gh-1459 ask #4). The headless `finally` then closes the session with
  the SEAL (`Session.seal`, gh-1589): after the usage fold + the
  job-board/obligations/subagent flushes (close order: drain → usage
  fold → seal → exit, the REPL teardown seals the same way), every writer
  observes the sealed session — late appends are DROPPED with one stderr
  warning per writer class, never written, so the session JSONL is a

  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +

  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`
  self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to) is EXEMPT from the
  cap — a deliberate agent-chosen cadence (night watch, periodic sweep)
  wakes forever, with a 30s cadence floor so a zero-delay re-schedule
  spin is still bounded like chatter; foreign agent chatter stays
  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`
  line per episode and a `wake_refused` receipt.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1941): the selected CodeMie project now rides EVERY model request.
  The header is baked into `Model.headers` only by the connect-time
  switches (gh-1809), so every other rebuild silently dropped
  `x-codemie-project` — and the backend bills a header-less request against
  the user's DEFAULT project (codemie-code `header-injection.plugin.ts`
  contract): the reported symptom is limit-exhausted from the exhausted
  default project despite picking a budgeted one. Rebuilds now re-resolve
  the project from the saved entry through one helper
  (`projectHeaderForBaseUrl`): the boot folder-state restore (JWT entries
  previously booted header-less — the SSO cookie patch was the only boot
  carrier), the session-resume re-apply (`_buildRestoredModel`), the
  roles-chain failover (`ModelRef.project`, mirroring the #964 authHeader
  leg), the roles-mode `/model` + settings-flow pins, and the generic
  `/provider` switch. The models list (`/llm_models`, SSO + JWT + guided
  setup + entry dispatch) and the quota adapter (dark until pinned) scope
  themselves to the same project, so display and billing can never diverge.
  Tests pin the header VALUE on the wire (real adapter over a fake
  endpoint) for the restored and failed-over models.
- feat(network): private networks created outside the app surface after
  sign-in. `GET /api/networks/mine` (fa_network#16) is synced into the
  wallet after OAuth/dev sign-in and both restore paths — best-effort,
  silent on older backends (404) and any failure, and never destructive.
  Synced memberships keep the server's name/class, preserve local
  passwords/join facts, and land without a password (the endpoint never
  returns one) until the first join. Entering such a network — sidebar,
===

## Summary

`schedule_message` (delayed timers) were scheduled into a **subagent's mailbox** instead of the caller's own (`main`) mailbox — both with the default recipient and with an explicit `to: <sessionId>/main`.

## Environment

- fa 1.0.659, macOS darwin/arm64
- Orchestrator session with a running `task`-spawned subagent (`qjs_race`) whose `task-result` had just been delivered into my context.

## Repro (from a live session log)

1. Spawn a background subagent (e.g. `qjs_race`); it completes and its `<task-result>` arrives.
2. Call `schedule_message` with `delay`/`text` only (default = own mailbox).
3. Observe the tool response: `scheduled 1792973362437462_000c_12yv1mk for ... — it will arrive as [scheduled] mail in 01a0f709-…/qjs_race` — **wrong mailbox** (expected `…/main`).
4. Retry with explicit `to: 01a0f709-…/main` — response again says `.../qjs_race`; the explicit override is ignored the same way.

## Observed consequences

- The misrouted timer auto-resumed the *completed* subagent (completed children are resumed by inbox mail), so `task_status` showed it running again (~10+ min after completion) and heartbeats kept arriving for a finished agent.
- The timer did eventually reach the orchestrator, but with sender `…/qjs_race: [scheduled]`, i.e. delivered via the wrong participant; the resumed agent also had to be told to stand down to prevent it from re-executing the timer's instructions (risk of duplicated side effects — in our case a duplicate release dispatch).
- `task_send` to the wrongly-resumed child reported `queued message for running subagent`, confirming the mailbox was active again.

## Suspicion

Recipient resolution for `schedule_message` appears to key off the most recent context participant (the task-result sender) rather than the calling agent's identity; the explicit `to:` override does not correct it.

## Expected

- Default recipient = the caller's own mailbox, always.
- Explicit `to:` must be honored verbatim.
- A scheduled message should never silently wake/resume a completed subagent unless explicitly addressed to it.

288-  /// (the hub's start block), [onSettled] when a job exits. [jobLogMaxBytes]
289-  /// and [onJobLogWarning] (issue #919) are merged into every start's
290-  /// options — the size ceiling and the low-disk warning channel; null
291-  /// bytes means the shells' built-in default. A caller's own options
292-  /// values take precedence over these session defaults.
293-  ShellJobRegistry({
294-    required this.env,
295-    this.onStart,
296-    this.onSettled,
297-    this.onStaleJobLog,
298-    this.jobLogMaxBytes,
299-    this.onJobLogWarning,
300-    this.jobLogDir,
301-    this.jobLogRedactor,
302-    this.maxRetainedExitedJobs = defaultMaxRetainedExitedJobs,
303-    DateTime? bootTime,
304-  }) : _bootTime = bootTime ?? DateTime.now();
305-
306-  /// How many exited jobs the registry retains (gh-1438 second tier).
307-  /// Production monitor sessions ran thousands of short-lived jobs and the
308-  /// grow-only list kept every entry — with its log text — for the process
309-  /// lifetime. Beyond the cap the oldest-settled entries are pruned (LRU by
310-  /// settle time); their log FILES stay on disk and exact-id lookups fall
311-  /// back to them ([prunedLogPath]/[tailFromLog], AC4). Running jobs are
312-  /// never pruned.
313-  static const defaultMaxRetainedExitedJobs = 100;
314-
315-  /// The exited-entry retention cap; see [defaultMaxRetainedExitedJobs].
316-  final int maxRetainedExitedJobs;
317-
318-  /// The environment jobs run in.
319-  final ExecutionEnv env;
320-
321-  /// Fires on every job exit — the host's terminal bookkeeping (job
322-  /// board, waiting row) hangs off it. Whether the MODEL is also told is
323-  /// the host's call, via [ShellJobEntry.notifyOnSettle] (issue #562).
324-  final void Function(ShellJobEntry job)? onSettled;
325-
326-  /// Fires when a job successfully starts (issue #277 task blocks).

**FOUND THE ZONE CAPTURE!**

```dart
unawaited(
 entry.setled.then((_) async {
 await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
 ...
 onSetled?.call(entry);
 }),
);
``

This `.then` is registered inside `ShellJobRegistry.start(...)` — i.e., **in the zone of the bash tool call that started the job**. If the bash tool call ran inside a CHILD's run (child zone), the settle callback — including `onSetled?.call(entry)` → CLI `_onShellJobSetled` → idle `_startRun(...)` → MAIN'S RUN — executes **INSIDE THE (long-finished) CHILD'S SUBAGENT ZONE**. Every tool call of that wake run — including `schedule_message` — reads `activeSubagentId()` == the child → gh-1947 EXACTLY: "keyed off the most recent context participant (the task-result sender)".

Wait — but does `entry.setled`'s listener really run in the registration zone? `entry.setled` — the ShellJob's settled future — `LocalShell`'s job — its `settled` completer completes from the process-exit handler — registered where `Process.start` ran — the CHILD zone too. `.then` on it → runs in the `.then` registration zone = the zone at `ShellJobRegistry.start` = the caller's zone = the CHILD's zone (for a child's bash call). YES.

Hmm — but ALSO: `_startRun` → `agent.prompt` → main's run continues on THIS zone — and EVERY await continuation of the whole main run stays in the child zone!!! (Zone is captured per continuation — since prompt's chain was ENTERED in the child zone, everything downstream runs there.) So the ENTIRE main wake run misattributes — schedule_message, reply (n/a), etc.

BUT — the ticket's repro step 1-2: "Spawn a background subagent (e.g. qjs_race); it completes and its task-result arrives. Call schedule_message..." — no bash job mentioned. Hmm. BUT the reproduction log is condensed; the agent in the release session had run MANY things. The `_startRun` from a shell-job settle inside qjs_race's zone → the reaction run → agent schedules → MISROUTE with response "in …/qjs_race" — and the agent's message says "Orchestrator session with a RUNNING task-spawned subagent (qjs_race) whose task-result had just been delivered into my context" — the agent's PERCEPTION (the transcript showed qjs_race's result recently) — while the ACTUAL zone leak came from wherever.

Hmm, wait — actually — hold on, is there an EVEN SIMPLER capture of the same shape for the TASK flow? `_onTaskJobCompleted` → `.listen` at boot — root ✓. What about `_waiting.push()`... no.

Hmm, what about **`TaskJobManager.completions` listener in the APP**: `_taskCompletionsSub = wired.taskConfig!.jobManager.completions.listen(_onTaskJobCompleted)` — registered in `_buildAgentAsync` — the app's session-open flow. IF the app opened THIS session while... no.

AND — **THE HEADLESS DRAIN**: `_finishHeadlessDrain` — "a job settle does bookeeping only" — after the fence. Fine.

So my PRIMARY leak candidate: `ShellJobRegistry.start`'s `entry.setled.then(...)` zone capture (child bash → main's later wake runs misattributed). Let me VERIFY EMPIRICALLY through the real CLI: spawn a child whose turn runs `bash` with `background: true` (or the child's bash gets auto-backgrounded? simpler: explicit background:true) → the child completes → the job settles (need the fake shell's job to settle) → `_onShellJobSetled` → `_startRun` (idle) → main schedules → assert the record.

The FakeCliIO harness: env has `UnavailableShell` — I need a shell whose `startShellJob` returns a job that settles ON DEMAND (like `_HangJob` but with a release). The child_wait test has `_HangShell`. I'll write a `_JobShell` with a setable job I can settle later.

Wait — actually — do CHILDREN even get the `bash` tool? coreTools includes bash (env-based). In the test env, `Shell` is provided via `MemoryExecutionEnv(shell:)` → builtin bash → registry created with env... The CLI's `_shellJobs` registry is created in services: `shellJobsFactory: (coreEnv) => ShellJobRegistry(env: coreEnv, onSetled: _onShellJobSetled)` — one REGISTRY for the whole CLI — children use the SAME registry (builtinTools(env...)). So a child's `bash background:true` → `_shellJobs.start` → the `.then` registers in THE CHILD'S ZONE. ✓.

Let me now ALSO reconsider whether the same zone-capture bug hits the TASK flow through a different registration... `_onTaskJobCompleted` — root. OK.

And hmm — ALSO the reverse shape: `_sterTuiMessages`... no.

Now — is the FIX in `ShellJobRegistry.start` (bind the settle continuation to the REGISTRY OWNER's zone — i.e., capture `Zone.current` AT REGISTRY CONSTRUCTION / capture the callback's zone) or in the CLI (`_startRun` should run main's runs in the ROOT zone — an identity-barier)? The ROBUST fix per the ticket's Expected: **recipient resolution must never key off a stale zone — the CALLER's identity must be captured where the run actually starts.** Multiple layers:

1. **`ShellJobRegistry`**: bind `onSetled` (and the whole settle continuation) to the zone captured at CONSTRUCTION time (host boot), not the starting call's zone. Same class of bug could bite `onStart`. This is the root cause of the leak.

2. **Defense in depth at the tool**: `scheduleMessageTool` — the response must name the RESOLVED `to`, and `senderMailbox` should be consulted only when the executing agent is genuinely a child. Hmm — but from the tool's view there's no other signal. That's a nice defensive check: `activeSubagentId()` is only trusted if that child is actually in flight on the executor (spawn or resume). In a legit child schedule, the child IS in flight (its own run encloses the call). In the leaked wake-run case, the child is completed → NOT in flight → resolve null → main. This kills the symptom even if other leaks exist.

3. **The response text**: report `to` (the actual recipient) — the honest reporting fix the ticket's AC2 demands.

Let me also check the APP's `scheduleSenderMailbox` for the same defense — the app has `_subagentManager` and... does the app have the executor? `_taskConfig.executor` — yes. The app closure could apply the same `isInFlight` guard. Hmm — but careful: gh-970's legit case — the child schedules DURING its run — `isInFlight` true (the run is enclosed). The resume case: `resumeChild` adds to `_resumesInFlight` + `_currentSubagentIds` — `isInFlight` true ✓. The BLOCKING-batch queued child (semaphore-waiting): `_currentSubagentIds.add(id)` happens AFTER semaphore acquire — a queued child's tools can't run yet ✓. So the guard is sound.

Hmm — but WAIT: is `TaskExecutor.isInFlight` exported/reachable? It's a method on TaskExecutor (public). The CLI has `_taskConfig.executor`. ✓.

Also — what about `Zone` capture in OTHER registries with the same shape? Let me grep for `.then((_)` + onSetled/onFired patterns... The scheduled queue's `_armAt` Timer — created in `_arm()` — called from `schedule()` — the TOOL CALL's zone!! `_timer = Timer(leg, () async { ... _deliverDue() ... })` — the timer callback runs in the ZONE WHERE `Timer` WAS CREATED — the scheduling call's zone — A CHILD'S ZONE (if a child scheduled)! Then `_deliverDue` → `_repo().send(...)` — delivers into mailboxes — fine — and `onFired` → CLI prints + `_pushScheduledStatus` — bookeeping ✓ no run start. So harmless-ish. BUT the receipt log writes via env — fine.

What about `SubagentHeartbeat._schedule` — Timer created at boot ✓ root.

OK also grep the CLI for other `whenComplete`/`.then` that call `_startRun`: `_inboxWakeRunning` cleanup (root), `settled.whenComplete` in `_startRun` (registered from the STARTING zone — the leaked child zone in the bug scenario — bookeeping only ✓), `_herdrRunIdle` ✓ bookeeping.

`_deliverHeartbeatDigest` — notify ← heartbeat timer (root) ✓.

`_onShellJobSetled` — the LEAK. Let me confirm by reading it and then write the failing test.

content.text: 14:## Unreleased

arguments.newText:
## Unreleased

- fix(#1947): `schedule_message` from the orchestrator no longer misroutes
  into a finished subagent's mailbox. A background shell job started by a
  CHILD registered its settle continuation inside the child's subagent
  zone; when the job settled after the child's run ended, the CLI's
  settle-wake (`_onShellJobSettled` → `_startRun`) started MAIN's reaction
  run still carrying the finished child's `activeSubagentId()`, and every
  identity consumer of that run misattributed it — the reported shape was
  a self-reminder scheduled "in <session>/<child>" that auto-resumed the
  completed child (duplicate-release risk). Three layers: the
  `ShellJobRegistry` now binds its settle continuation to the
  construction-time (boot) zone (`_bootZone.run`), both hosts'
  `scheduleSenderMailbox` wiring trusts the zone scope only while the
  child is genuinely in flight on the session executor
  (`TaskExecutor.isInFlight`), and the tool response names the RECIPIENT
  the record carries — an explicit `to:` used to be shadowed in the reply
  by the sender's mailbox, which read as "the override was ignored" even
  when it was honored. E2E repro drives the real AgentCli
  (test/cli/agent_cli_schedule_recipient_test.dart) plus a registry-level
  zone pin (test/tools/shell_job_settle_zone_test.dart).
- fix(#1941): the selected CodeMie project now rides EVERY model request.

arguments.content:
### What changed
Fixed `schedule_message` recipient resolution so an orchestrator's timers can no longer land in a (finished) subagent's mailbox, and made the tool response name the recipient the record actually carries.

### Root cause
A background shell job started by a CHILD registered its settle continuation inside the child's subagent zone. When the job settled after the child's run had ended, the CLI's settle-wake (`_onShellJobSettled` → `_startRun`) started the MAIN reaction run still carrying the finished child's `activeSubagentId()` — every `schedule_message` in that run self-addressed to the child (and the response printed the child's mailbox even when an explicit `to:` was honored, which read as "override ignored").

### Key decisions
- `ShellJobRegistry` binds its settle continuation to the construction-time (boot) zone (`_bootZone.run`), never to the zone of the `bash` call that started the job — the leak's root fix.
- Defense in depth: both hosts' `scheduleSenderMailbox` wiring (CLI `_childSenderMailbox`, app host builder) trust the zone scope only while that child is genuinely in flight on the session executor (`TaskExecutor.isInFlight`) — any future stale-zone capture degrades to the caller's own (main) mailbox, never to a dead child's. The gh-970 case (a live child scheduling its own reminder) keeps the child identity.
- The tool response now prints ` in <resolved recipient>` from the record's `to` (explicit `to:` wins, then the caller's mailbox); the `scheduled <id> for ` prefix consumed by the obligations ledger stays byte-stable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_schedule_recipient_test.dart \
          test/tools/shell_job_settle_zone_test.dart
dart test test/messaging/ test/task/ test/tools/
```
The e2e test reproduces the ticket through the real AgentCli: a child starts a background bash job, finishes; the job settles afterwards and wakes MAIN, whose scripted reaction schedules with no `to` — the record must land in `<session>/main` (it landed in `<session>/qjs_race` before the fix).

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHILD[child run: bash background:true] -->|job starts in child zone| REG[ShellJobRegistry.start]
  CHILD -->|run ends| DONE[child completed]
  REG -->|settle continuation| ZONE[boot zone _bootZone.run]
  DONE -->|job settles later| ZONE
  ZONE --> WAKE[_onShellJobSettled → _startRun: MAIN run]
  WAKE -->|activeSubagentId() = child ✗ before / null ✓ after| TOOL[schedule_message]
  TOOL -->|guard: isInFlight(child) false → sender null| MAIN[record to: session/main]
```

</details>

arguments.text: gh-1947 root cause (fix 5941833): ShellJobRegistry.start registered the job's settle continuation in the CALLING bash call's zone — a background job started by a subagent carried its onSettled into the child's subagent zone, so a job settling after the child finished started the CLI settle-wake (_onShellJobSettled → _startRun → agent.prompt) with activeSubagentId() still naming the dead child; the whole MAIN wake run (schedule_message self-mailbox resolution included) attributed to the child (timers landed in <session>/<child>, auto-resuming it). Fix layers: (1) registry binds the settle continuation to its construction-time boot zone (_bootZone.run); (2) both hosts' scheduleSenderMailbox closures trust the zone scope only while TaskExecutor.isInFlight(id) — stale zones degrade to main; (3) the schedule_message response names the record's `to` (explicit to: was shadowed by the sender in the reply). Test: test/cli/agent_cli_schedule_recipient_test.dart drives the REAL AgentCli (FakeCliIO + _SettleableJobShell whose jobs settle on demand); zone pin at test/tools/shell_job_settle_zone_test.dart. LESSON: any .then/whenComplete/listener registered during a tool call inherits that call's zone forever — host callbacks that can START RUNS must be bound to the boot zone, and zone-scoped identity consumers need an in-flight liveness check.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1947): `schedule_message` from the orchestrator no longer misroutes
  into a finished subagent's mailbox. A background shell job started by a
  CHILD registered its settle continuation inside the child's subagent
  zone; when the job settled after the child's run ended, the CLI's
  settle-wake (`_onShellJobSettled` → `_startRun`) started MAIN's reaction
  run still carrying the finished child's `activeSubagentId()`, and every
  identity consumer of that run misattributed it — the reported shape was
  a self-reminder scheduled "in <session>/<child>" that auto-resumed the
  completed child (duplicate-release risk). Three layers: the
  `ShellJobRegistry` now binds its settle continuation to the
  construction-time (boot) zone (`_bootZone.run`), both hosts'
  `scheduleSenderMailbox` wiring trusts the zone scope only while the
  child is genuinely in flight on the session executor
  (`TaskExecutor.isInFlight`), and the tool response names the RECIPIENT
  the record carries — an explicit `to:` used to be shadowed in the reply
  by the sender's mailbox, which read as "the override was ignored" even
  when it was honored. E2E repro drives the real AgentCli
  (test/cli/agent_cli_schedule_recipient_test.dart) plus a registry-level
  zone pin (test/tools/shell_job_settle_zone_test.dart).
- fix(#1941): the selected CodeMie project now rides EVERY model request.
  The header is baked into `Model.headers` only by the connect-time
  switches (gh-1809), so every other rebuild silently dropped
  `x-codemie-project` — and the backend bills a header-less request against
  the user's DEFAULT project (codemie-code `header-injection.plugin.ts`
  contract): the reported symptom is limit-exhausted from the exhausted

2.5. **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: if the task ships a runnable verifier, test, or entry point the grader will call, run THAT command the way the grader will — neutral cwd (`cd /` — a different working directory, never the session cwd), fresh subprocess, clean env (no session-exported vars) — and compare stdout, stderr, and exit code against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` item to fix before finalizing. The ledger row for the main artifact uses this invocation as its `command:`.
2.6. **Conformance coverage** — applies ONLY when the final claim includes behavioral conformance: "matches the reference/specification", parity with an existing implementation, protocol/format compliance — any domain. Happy-path agreement certifies nothing about rejection paths or option combinations: two implementations agreeing on every well-formed input can still diverge exactly where one of them must say no. A conformance item counts as verified only when the checklist also quotes **negative and combination checks**, each one actually run and quoted in its ledger row: inputs that must be rejected or must error, combinations of incompatible/mutually exclusive options that must be refused, empty and corrupt inputs, boundary values, "must NOT work" / "must not find" cases — alongside the happy paths. A blanket "everything matches" without such coverage is not verified: mark the item `fail` and run the missing cases.
3. **Fix every unmet item** — a failed item is fixed and re-verified. Fix attempts are bounded: don't spiral on one dead end — switch approach.
4. **Final state is the deliverable** — never uninstall, stop, reset, or clean up what you produced while finalizing. Verification steps must be read-only or additive (a smoke probe, a curl, a diff) — never destructive. Cleanup happens only if the task explicitly requires it. ❌ Wrong: "verified, then reset to a clean state so the checker's commands run exactly as written" — the produced state no longer exists at grading, and that is a `fail`, not a clean handoff.

**Feasibility before commitment.** Before starting any step whose cost can dominate the remaining budget (from-source builds, large downloads, brute-force searches), estimate its duration and compare it against the time-left notices. If the estimate exceeds the budget, switch to a cheaper strategy that still satisfies the task (binary packages, targeted sub-builds, reduced scope the task allows) — or, when no satisfying strategy fits, the next-best partial — never gamble the whole window on a path you already know cannot finish.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Archive extraction is complete** — after extracting a provided/downloaded archive into a target directory, diff the archive's full listing against the extracted tree (`unzip -l <archive>` / `tar -tf <archive>` vs `ls -R` of the target, or `find <target> -type f`); every entry — including root-level files with no extension and no obvious purpose (`file_id.diz`, `README`, `LICENSE`, version stamps) — must be present. A partial extraction is a `fail` item.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed). The check runs against the state you leave behind: a file that existed mid-run but is deleted at finalization is a `fail` — final state is the deliverable (step 4).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.
